anomalies.observed: R7's pull-up/bias resistor is connected between the T3 gate net /G_{RPP} and the fused input net /+24V_{F}, which is also T3's source. The zener D3 (anode on /G_{RPP}, cathode on GND) is the only other connection to the gate. The gate therefore sits at the source potential through R7 and is never pulled toward GND, so T3 (P-channel, source on the input) stays off whenever 24 V is applied. The reverse-polarity path to +24V is blocked.
anomalies.expected: For a P-channel reverse-polarity switch with source on the fused input, the gate resistor should go from gate to GND and the zener should clamp gate-to-source. The spec describes T3 as a switching element with its gate driven through a 100 Ω resistor and a pre-driver transistor, and it names the input protection as part of the design. It does not describe this input-protection gate network.
anomalies.impact: If the topology is as drawn, T3 never conducts and the 24 V input cannot reach the +24V bulk rail, so the buck regulator, pumps and valve would be unpowered. If the reference design is the same, the protection is non-functional.

anomalies.observed: The main-pump MOSFET gate net /G_{PUMP} has a 10 kΩ pull-up to +3V3 (R5). It has no pull-down, although the other low-side MOSFET gates on this board (ATO, R12) are pulled down to GND. With the gate pulled high and the ESP32 pin (IO10) high-impedance during boot, the 24 V main pump is driven on by default.
anomalies.expected: A low-side N-channel pump switch should default to off, with its gate pulled to GND, so that the pump does not start on reset or during boot.
anomalies.impact: The main circulation pump may run at power-up or reset before firmware takes control, which could be a safety or water-handling issue.

parsed.summary: The reverse-polarity network around T3 is wired with R7 from the gate to the source and D3 from the gate to GND, so T3 is held off and the 24 V input cannot reach the board. The R5 pull-up on the main-pump gate is a weaker concern. The rest of the power, sensing and isolation wiring is consistent with the specification.
